subject: UK IDTA: evidence phasing, embargo clauses & TIA acceptance criteria
messages:

Cc: legal@cardiahealth.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: UK IDTA - evidence phasing and embargo clause question

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. CardiaHealth is ready to move forward with a pilot but our legal/privacy team needs to lock the UK IDTA (and associated TIA/DTIA evidence) before procurement signs off. Two quick asks so we can scope the internal review: 

1) Evidence phasing: can Redwood deliver evidence in two tranches (Phase 1 = architecture diagrams, SCCs mapping, list of subprocessors; Phase 2 = sampled attestation artifacts and redacted logs)? Our security team needs Phase 1 by the time we start the procurement sprint.

2) Embargo clause/UK Addendum: the Cardia legal team is concerned about raw log disclosures when the UK IDTA requires demonstration of controls. Will Redwood accept a restricted (redacted & time-limited) evidence access arrangement or do you require raw log delivery?

We attached the Cardia TIA request form and would like to confirm acceptance criteria for Phase 1 so our security reviewers can proceed.

Can you confirm a proposed delivery cadence (dates) and what artifacts Redwood will include in each phase?

Best,
Elena Soto
Sr. Privacy Lead
CardiaHealth

Attachments: Cardia_TIA_request_form.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@cardiahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: UK IDTA - evidence phasing and embargo clause question

Elena —

Thanks, and great to hear Cardia is ready to move. We can absolutely support a phased evidence approach. Proposed plan below (we can tighten dates once you confirm internal stakeholders):

Phase 1 (required for procurement sprint) — deliver by 2026-09-03:
- High-level architecture diagram showing processing locations and data flows
- SCCs mapping worksheet (CSV) that ties clauses to our controls (see attached)
- Current subprocessors list + brief roles
- TIA request form, completed (we attached a pre-populated copy)

Phase 2 (attestation & sampled artifacts) — deliver by 2026-09-17:
- Redacted sample audit logs (time-bounded) and a short write-up of retention/rotation policies
- Signed attestation from our infra/security team confirming controls in scope for the TIA
- Screenshots and sanitized outputs of audit dashboards where applicable

Regarding the embargo/raw logs question: we do not provide unfettered raw log dumps. Standard practice for UK IDTA/UK addenda is:
- We can provide time-bounded, redacted log excerpts and verifiable artifacts (hashes, screenshots) that demonstrate controls without exposing PII or secret material.
- For highly sensitive requests we offer a sealed-access workflow (secure share + NDA-addendum) and a Redacted Evidence Packet.

Next steps we'd like from Cardia:
1) Confirm Phase 1 acceptance criteria and whether legal wants sealed-access for Phase 2 artifacts.
2) Confirm a single point of contact for procurement sign-off (name + email).
3) Confirm whether your legal team requires a doc-level amendment to the UK IDTA regarding embargoed evidence.

Attachments: SCCs-mapping-worksheet.csv (pre-populated), Cardia_TIA_request_form.pdf (filled draft)

If that looks good I'll loop in Kimberly for formal attestation language and Logan for the evidence delivery timeline.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

On Sun, Aug 30, 2026 at 10:04 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Elena —
> 
> Thanks, and great to hear Cardia is ready to move. We can absolutely support a phased evidence approach. Proposed plan below ...

Elena / Marissa — some specifics from a controls and legal perspective: 

- Subprocessors: we'll provide an up-to-date CSV with subprocessors, region of processing, and the contractual role (processor/subprocessor). We currently use encryption-at-rest + KMS separation for customer keys (we can provide KMS vendor + key-rotation cadence).

- Audit artifacts: we can provide redacted log excerpts that show the event timeline, user-ids replaced with pseudonyms, and hashes for integrity verification. We cannot export raw, unredacted logs that would include end-user PII or full session payloads.

- UK IDTA / Addendum language: our legal team is willing to add an explicit clause that allows for "sealed evidence access" — a temporary, credentialed access window where Cardia's authorized reviewer can view redacted artifacts in a secure workspace. This clause will include a limited time window (e.g., 7 days) and a prohibition on copying raw logs.

- TIA acceptance criteria (proposed):
  1) Phase 1 artifacts received and validated against the SCCs mapping
  2) Phase 2 redacted samples match the logging/retention claims in the TIA form
  3) Signed attestation from Redwood infra/security team (we will provide standard language)

Operational note: delivery will be via a secured GDrive folder with restricted links; for sealed-access we will create a temporary project folder with view-only, watermarked PDF artifacts. If Cardia requires an on-site/air-gapped inspection we will need to escalate to an enterprise agreement.

I will draft the attestation and a UK IDTA addendum paragraph for the sealed-access workflow and share by EOD 2026-09-02.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
